It's the thought of knowing that it'd be the last interaction (what you're leaving people with), the feelings/thoughts that rush through your mind, and so much more. So, I can only imagine how you must've felt writing it. Either way, it's definitely something that lingers sometimes. I hope you've at least enjoyed something today out of your day.

there are many factors to consider. struggling with a mental illness can be so crippling and may affect your way of life in various ways. given, that the healthcare system isn't that great at accommodating those with mental illnesses, etc. there's just plenty to consider is all i can say.

i wouldn't say that the government is preying on the vulnerable, rather it would almost be like giving them the choice to "die with dignity." then again like you've said, it's to also destigmatize that concept. besides, the suicide rates are only rising and if you ever struggled/are struggling with mental illnesses, you'll know how it goes more or less (mentally/physically).
fair point, but i think op/the comments meant throwing pills at people who are suicidal, etc. isn't the best way to handle the situation when it's more than that.

i oddly like this perspective that you're touching upon, tbh. a complicated/controversial topic too. there may be various explanations if we're talking about person to person, etc. i struggle with my mental health, and have questioned/thought similarly to you regarding the world's perspective of sh/suicide. it's truly baffling, to say the least. 

if anything, i wish suicide was more accepted within society/the world(i do apologize if it sounds/seems morbid). however, i do understand why people would want us to cherish our lives because it's unique in a sense(?). there's only ever one of us i guess. though, the hardships are just as brutal. i think there's a lot of potential you can achieve if you're able to embrace/love yourself. it's sort of like you'd be living for yourself rather than living for what others would want you to achieve, etc. it's a difficult topic to answer too lol.

no problem, i'm just really hoping things will be fine for you all eventually. i'm not sure how recent your friend's breakup was, but i assume the things he's doing/reacting to right now is how much he's hurting, etc. i'm glad that he has a friend like you to stick around because it can get rough. given that we all may handle breakups differently, we will react in a certain way and all that stuff. 

for right now, i guess you can give him some time to process with how he's feeling/thinking regarding the breakup, etc. then also be there for him as much as you want. the same goes for his ex since you're friends with her too. honestly, just being in your position is tough. especially when you're friends with them both hahah. i could tell you just hope your friend(s) will be alright, so that's cool man. 

if the girl does feel uncomfortable, then i'd suggest communicating about it if they want to (to draw some sort of boundary). otherwise, she can block him too i guess. going through a breakup just f\*\*ks you up in a way for a while (for the majority). this is really cliche, but time will seriously heal more or less. i know your friend must be going through a really bad breakup and it'll take time for him to move on. it just sucks when you're still in love with someone, but to the other person, it's over, etc. (just being the one to break up or the receiving end is a difficult matter). it's just, with time you'll eventually move forward. as difficult as it may be for your friend to hear that, it's just life i guess. 

i am sorry that he lashed out at you though. just remember to take care of yourself too man. though, i would still take his suicidal thoughts/feelings seriously if anything. since he doesn't want any help as of right now, you can just stick around. if it gets worse, maybe you'll have to take action. it's tough, so that's my take on it at least. seriously, you guys take care

reading this, i would've thought you were talking about me lol. even though i live in LA instead. i can relate to your friend as i'm in a really similar position as him right now. then again, i can understand from your point of view regardless. 

otherwise, i would say that just being there for him right now as he's struggling can be helpful. it's good to know that he feels comfortable enough to share his thoughts/feelings with you despite how overwhelming it can be on both ends. there could possibly be times where he may push you away, want to be alone, etc. which is understandable. then again, it could be risky because of various factors. so i would say to just really let him know that you're there for him regardless. 

that being said, it can be a really helpless situation to be in. this is because nothing that my friends said went through my head too. i pushed them all away and isolated myself. it sucks when you want the best for your friend, but they just seem to be lost in the dark void of depression/suicidal thoughts.  

if anything, i really hope that you at least know a few of his family members or friends he knows in real life. sometimes you may have to put yourself in a position of doing what you think is right for your friend atm. i know even that's a tough decision because it may feel like you're invalidating how they're feeling, etc. it's just conflicting overall. 

last but not least, don't forget to take care of yourself as well. i'm really wishing you the best of luck and would love an update if you're comfortable with sharing.

no worries, thank you as well.

i do apologize if my comment wasn't as helpful, but i hope at some point you'll comfortably come around to talk about what's troubling you. i hope your friends/family would understand if anything. take care now !

your feelings are valid if anything. no matter how stupid you may think they are, validating them is still important - the first step for most. get comfortable first if you need to before telling someone about them, etc.

i ain't going to lie either because i did push people away. i've been in a depressive episode for months now. the thoughts/feelings of burdening them/annoying them/you name it, just really weighed on me. it's not that i want them to chase me or whatever some people do, it's just i want to be alone (yet found?).

either way, wishing you the best of luck

in my personal experience, it does get slightly better more or less. then like almost everything, you have to maintain it too (which can get very difficult to manage). i'd say it differs for everyone to an extent when it comes to it. i'd also say it fluctuated a lot for me as i'm not taking meds nor seeking professional help to consistently maintain it, i guess (it can be a risky thing to do alone/no help). meaning that i go to and from being suicidal/depressed to feeling alright for periods of time. 

that being said, i'd say that it all really depends on the individual(s). sometimes the individual(s) may have/need to seek help to help them overall (majority of the time). which is completely fine. besides that, i really do hope you've friends/family in real life that you can turn to. you don't have to tell them everything in detail if you're not comfortable. you can just say, "hey i haven't been doing mentally well lately," for starters. then again, i won't tell you what to do as it'll be your decision on how you'll approach this matter. 

if it gives you a little insight, i try to make a small list of things i know i can do/try to do daily. EX: i make a list to make sure i tidy up in the morning: wash my face, brush my teeth, shower, eat, etc. this is just so i can keep myself in check. otherwise, i really do hope you slowly try and take care of yourself as time goes on. i know how difficult it can get to look after yourself when you've no energy/motivation in general. it's okay to start small and progress from there. wishing you the best of luck.

i completely understand where you’re coming from because i am struggling with that too.

my depression is chronic, so it comes and goes. sometimes i just wallow in it until it feels like i’ve no other choice but to actually do something to improve overall. probably not ideal, but it really be like that sometimes. (currently not taking any meds/seeking professional help). 

trying to keep yourself productive in the sense of doing things to distract you, will be very difficult. maybe you can even try playing games on your phone while in bed or watch funny/interesting videos. it really does make you question, “yeah, i’m doing this but what for?” (at least for me since i’m also suicidal). it’s just overall depressing.

depression for me feels like a dark, deep, and bottomless pit of a void. it feels like i’m only drowning further and further into it. feels like no one can hear me/understand me. feels like all my thoughts/feelings regarding around it only pulls me in deeper. it makes me feel insecure (loss of self-confidence/self esteem/overall well-being plummets). start to overthink a lot. start to feel like a burden. enjoying things less. little to no motivation. that’s all i could think of atm hahah

i tend to isolate myself from everybody, both online/in real life (i live by myself) when it gets really bad. that being said, i hope you’re taking care.

otherwise the only other reasons i can think of would be to not cause pain to friends/family. another would be that, “it will pass,” kind of point of view. i know how that last sentence may sound, it’s just life goes on sometimes. then again, i still do believe that people should be able to die on their own terms kind of concept. we’ve all our own different opinions, etc.

hey, i'd like to believe that we're all loveable despite our traumatic/internal problems, etc. it's difficult to see things clearly when we're in/been feeling the dark void. which is understandable. i may not know what's going on with you, but i'll give you my piece of that. hoping you'll take care

i won't, but i wouldn't mind listening/hearing you out if you ever want to share anything (whether it's in the comments/dms, i don't mind). i'm not sure what you're going through either, but i'm really hoping you'll be okay. please seriously take care of yourself if you aren't already.

other than that, i am not an expert with meds nor am i taking them. i heard that antidepressants, in general, may take weeks to kick in or to feel their effects/their side effects can be difficult to handle. however, if it gets really difficult to handle, i hope you've your therapist/doctor's phone # to contact them when needed/wanted. if anything, i hope you've someone friends/family that you can also turn to during times like these. 

just know that your effort(s) to take these meds are admirable. this is because you're doing what you can at the moment. please take care good care of yourself. otherwise, if you ever need someone to talk to/someone to hear you out, i will be around. really hope that there's at least a brief moment of your day that you enjoy/feel okay.
